title.en: Volume 61 Biographies 26: Yu Wenshu, Guo Yan

sentences.zh: 宇文述宇文述，字伯通，代郡武川人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wen Shu—Yu Wen Shu, style name Botong, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu, whose courtesy name was Botong, came from Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 本姓破野頭，役屬鮮卑俟豆歸，後從其主為宇文氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Poyetou; he was a dependent of the Xianbei chief Sihou Dougui, and later followed his lord in taking the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had originally borne the name Poyetou and served the Xianbei leader Sihou Dougui; they later adopted the surname Yuwen when they followed their lord.

sentences.zh: 父盛，周上柱國。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was Senior Pillar of State in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng had held the rank of Senior Pillar of State under the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 述少驍銳，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Shu in youth was fierce and sharp, skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wenshu was bold and keen, and adept with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 年十一時，有相者謂述曰：「公子善自愛，後當位極人臣。

translations.literal: At age eleven, a physiognomist said to Shu: 'Young lord, take good care of yourself—you will later reach the highest rank among ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: When he was eleven, a fortune-teller told him, 'Young sir, cherish yourself well; one day you will stand at the pinnacle of ministerial power.'

sentences.zh: 」周武帝時，以父軍功，起家拜開府。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, through his father's military merit, he began his career and was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Zhou, he entered official life on the strength of his father's military service and was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 述性恭謹沈密，周大塚宰宇文護甚愛之，以本官領護親信。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was respectful, cautious, and deep and reserved; the Great Chief Minister of Zhou, Yuwen Hu, greatly favored him and had him, in his existing office, lead the guard of trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was respectful, cautious, and reserved by nature. Yuwen Hu, the Great Chief Minister of Zhou, took a strong liking to him and, while keeping him in his existing post, put him in charge of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 及帝親總萬機，召為左宮伯，累遷英果中大夫，賜爵博陵郡公，尋改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor personally took charge of all affairs of state, Shu was summoned as Left Palace Baron, was repeatedly promoted to Valiant Fruit Grand Master, was granted the title Duke of Boling Commandery, and soon had his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor began to rule in person, Wenshu was summoned to serve as Left Palace Baron. He rose in stages to Valiant Fruit Grand Master, was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling, and soon had his title changed to Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂相州，述以行軍總管率步騎三千，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yu Chi Kuo raised rebellion at Xiang Province; Shu, as campaign commander-in-chief, led three thousand infantry and cavalry and followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jian was still Chancellor, Yuwen Jue rebelled at Xiang Province. Wenshu, serving as campaign commander-in-chief, led three thousand foot and horse soldiers under Wei Xiaokuan to strike him.

sentences.zh: 軍至河陽，迥遣將李俊攻懷州，述別擊俊軍，破之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Heyang, Kuo sent the general Li Jun to attack Huai Province; Shu separately attacked Jun's army and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Heyang. Jue sent the general Li Jun to attack Huai Prefecture, but Wenshu struck Jun's force on a separate axis and routed it.

sentences.zh: 又與諸將擊尉惇於永橋，述先鋒陷陣，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: He again joined the generals in attacking Yu Dun at Yong Bridge; Shu as vanguard broke the enemy line, and captives and severed heads were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the other generals in attacking Yu Dun at Yong Bridge. Wenshu led the van, broke through the enemy formation, and took a great many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 平尉迥，每戰有功，超拜上柱國，進爵褒國公，賜縑三千匹。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi Kuo was pacified, in every battle he had merit; he was specially promoted to Senior Pillar of State, advanced in title to Duke of the State of Bao, and granted three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: After Jue's rebellion was put down, Wenshu distinguished himself in battle after battle. He was promoted out of turn to Senior Pillar of State, raised to Duke of Bao, and rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，複以行軍總管率眾三萬，自六合而濟。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, he again served as campaign commander-in-chief, leading an army of thirty thousand, and crossed from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he again served as campaign commander-in-chief, leading thirty thousand men across the river from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 時韓擒、賀若弼兩軍趣丹陽，述進據石頭，以為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Han Qin and He Ruo Bi were pressing toward Danyang; Shu advanced and seized Shitou as a supporting demonstration of force.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qin and He Ruo Bi were then driving on Danyang with two armies, while Wenshu advanced to hold Shitou and provide a supporting threat.

sentences.zh: 陳主既擒，而蕭瓛、蕭岩據東吳之地，擁兵拒守。

translations.literal: After the Chen ruler had been captured, Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan held the lands of Eastern Wu, mustering troops to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Chen ruler had been taken, Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan still held the eastern Wu region with armed forces and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 述領行軍總管元契、張默言等討之，水陸兼進。

translations.literal: Shu led the campaign commanders Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others to attack them, advancing by both water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu led the campaign commanders Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others against them, pressing forward by land and sea together.

sentences.zh: 落叢公燕榮以舟師自海至，亦受述節度。

translations.literal: Duke of Luocong Yan Rong came by sea with a fleet and also came under Shu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rong, Duke of Luocong, arrived by sea with a naval force and likewise placed himself under Wenshu's command.

sentences.zh: 上下詔曰：「公鴻勳大業，名高望重，奉國之誠，久所知悉。

translations.literal: Above and below an edict said: 'Lord, your great merit and great achievement, your high name and heavy reputation, and your loyalty in serving the state have long been fully known.'
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict declared, 'Your great achievements and towering reputation, and your long-proven loyalty to the state, are well known to Us.'

sentences.zh: 金陵之寇，既已清蕩，而吳會之地，東路為遙，蕭岩、蕭瓛，並在其處。

translations.literal: The bandits of Jinling have already been swept clean, but the lands of Wu and Kuai lie far along the eastern route; Xiao Yan and Xiao Kan are both there.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy at Jinling has already been cleared away, but Wu and Kuai lie far down the eastern route, and both Xiao Yan and Xiao Kan are there.

sentences.zh: 公率將戎旅，撫慰彼方，振揚國威，宣佈朝化。

translations.literal: Lord, lead your armed hosts, comfort and reassure that region, display the state's majesty, and proclaim the court's transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your troops there, pacify that region, display the majesty of the state, and spread the court's civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 以公明略，乘勝而往，風行電掃，自當稽服。

translations.literal: With your clear strategy, go forth riding victory; like wind moving and lightning sweeping, they will naturally submit in prostration.
translations.idiomatic: With your wise strategy, advance on the momentum of victory. Like wind and lightning you will sweep them away, and they will surely bow in submission.

sentences.zh: 若使干戈不用，黎庶獲安，方副朕懷，公之力也。

translations.literal: If arms need not be used and the common people gain peace, that will match Our heart—it will be through your power.
translations.idiomatic: If war can be avoided and the people brought to peace, that will fulfill Our wish—and it will be your doing.'

sentences.zh: 」陳永新侯陳君范自晉陵奔瓛，並軍合勢。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yongxin of Chen, Chen Junfan, fled from Jinling to join Kan, and their armies united their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junfan, Marquis of Yongxin, fled from Jinling to join Kan, and their forces united.

sentences.zh: 見述軍且至，瓛懼，立柵于晉陵城東，又絕塘道，留兵拒述。

translations.literal: Seeing that Shu's army was about to arrive, Kan was afraid; he built palisades east of Jinling city, also cut the embankment road, and left troops to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan saw Wenshu's army approaching, he grew afraid. He built palisades east of Jinling, cut the embankment road, and left troops to hold Wenshu off.

sentences.zh: 瓛自義興入太湖，圖掩述後。

translations.literal: Kan himself entered Tai Lake from Yixing, intending to strike at Shu's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Kan himself entered Lake Tai from Yixing, planning to take Wenshu from behind.

sentences.zh: 述進破其柵，回兵擊瓛，大敗之，斬瓛司馬曹勒叉。

translations.literal: Shu advanced, broke his palisades, turned his army to strike Kan, and inflicted a great defeat, beheading Kan's Chief Clerk Cao Lecha.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu advanced, broke through the palisades, wheeled about to strike Kan, and routed him decisively, beheading Kan's chief clerk Cao Lecha.

sentences.zh: 前軍複陷吳州，瓛以餘眾保包山，燕榮擊破之。

translations.literal: The vanguard again took Wu Province; Kan with his remaining troops held Mount Bao, and Yan Rong attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard took Wu Prefecture as well. Kan held Mount Bao with his remaining men, but Yan Rong attacked and broke him.

sentences.zh: 述進至奉公埭，蕭岩、陳君範等以會稽請降。

translations.literal: Shu advanced to Fenggong Dam; Xiao Yan, Chen Junfan, and others offered to surrender through Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu advanced to Fenggong Dam, where Xiao Yan, Chen Junfan, and others offered to surrender through Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 述許之，二人面縛路左，吳會悉平。

translations.literal: Shu granted it; the two men bound themselves face-forward on the left of the road, and Wu and Kuai were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu accepted. The two men bound themselves and presented themselves by the roadside, and Wu and Kuai were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功拜一子開府，賜物三千段，拜安州總管。

translations.literal: For his merit one son was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, he was granted three thousand lengths of goods, and he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: For his service one of his sons was appointed Grand Master of the Palace, he received three thousand lengths of goods as reward, and he was made Commander-in-Chief of An Province.

sentences.zh: 時晉王廣鎮揚州，甚善於述，欲述近己，因奏為壽州刺史總管。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Yangzhou and was very friendly with Shu; wishing to have Shu near himself, he therefore memorialized to have him made Inspector-General of Shou Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Guang was then posted at Yangzhou and was on excellent terms with Wenshu. Wanting him close at hand, the prince had him appointed Inspector-General of Shou Province.

sentences.zh: 王時陰有奪宗之志，請計於述，述曰：「皇太子失愛已久，令德不聞於天下。

translations.literal: The Prince at that time secretly harbored the ambition to seize the heirship and asked Shu for a plan. Shu said: 'The Crown Prince has long lost favor, and his fine virtue is not heard of throughout the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: The prince secretly harbored the ambition to seize the succession and asked Wenshu for counsel. Wenshu said, 'The crown prince has long fallen from favor, and his virtues are not spoken of throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 大王仁孝著稱，才能蓋世，數經將領，深有大功。

translations.literal: Great King, your benevolence and filial piety are renowned, your talent surpasses the age, you have repeatedly led armies, and you have deep and great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is famed for benevolence and filial piety, your talent surpasses the age, you have repeatedly commanded armies, and your achievements are great.

sentences.zh: 主上之與內宮，鹹所鍾愛，四海之望，實歸於大王。

translations.literal: The sovereign and the inner palace alike cherish you; the hopes of the four seas truly rest on Great King.
translations.idiomatic: Both the emperor and the inner palace favor you, and the hopes of the empire truly rest upon Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 然廢立者，國家之大事，處人父子骨肉之間，誠非易謀也。

translations.literal: Yet deposition and establishment are great affairs of state, situated between father and son and flesh and bone—it is truly not easy to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Yet deposition and enthronement are great affairs of state, and they touch the bonds between father and son and between flesh and blood. They are truly not easy to plot.

sentences.zh: 然能移主上者，唯楊素耳。

translations.literal: Yet the one who can move the sovereign is only Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the only man who can sway the emperor is Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素之謀者，唯其弟約。

translations.literal: Of Su's counselors, only his younger brother Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Of Su's counselors, only his younger brother Yue matters.

sentences.zh: 述雅知約，請朝京師，與約相見，共圖廢立。

translations.literal: Shu was on close terms with Yue; he asked to go to the capital, meet with Yue, and together plot deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was on close terms with Yue. He asked leave to go to the capital, meet Yue, and plot the succession together.'

sentences.zh: 」晉王大悅，多齎金寶，資述入關。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was greatly pleased and sent much gold and treasure to supply Shu for entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin was delighted and sent a great store of gold and jewels to fund Wenshu's journey to the capital.

sentences.zh: 述數請約，盛陳器玩，與之酣暢，因而共博，每佯不勝，所齎金寶盡輸之。

translations.literal: Shu repeatedly invited Yue, lavishly displayed vessels and curios, drank deeply with him, and then gambled together; each time he pretended not to win, and all the gold and treasure he had brought was lost to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu invited Yue again and again, displayed fine vessels and curios, drank freely with him, and then gambled. Each time he feigned defeat until all the gold and jewels he had brought had passed to Yue.

sentences.zh: 約所得既多，稍以謝述。

translations.literal: When Yue's gains were already many, he gradually began to thank Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue had won a great deal, he began to thank Wenshu in turn.

sentences.zh: 述因曰：「此晉王之賜，令述與公為歡樂耳。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon said: 'This is the Prince of Jin's gift, sent so that Shu and you, sir, might have pleasure together.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu then said, 'These were gifts from the Prince of Jin, sent so that you and I might enjoy ourselves together.'

sentences.zh: 」約大驚曰：「何為者？

translations.literal: Yue was greatly startled and said: 'What is the meaning of this?'
translations.idiomatic: Yue was astonished and asked, 'What does this mean?'

sentences.zh: 」述因為王申意。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon conveyed the Prince's intent on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu then explained the prince's intentions on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 約然其說，退言於素，素亦從之。

translations.literal: Yue approved of his argument, withdrew and spoke to Su, and Su also followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue accepted the plan, spoke of it to Su in private, and Su agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 於是素每與述謀事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su frequently plotted affairs together with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Su and Wenshu plotted together at every turn.

sentences.zh: 晉王與述情好益密，命述子士及尚南陽公主，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin and Shu grew ever closer in affection; he ordered Shu's son Shiji to marry the Princess of Nanyang, and rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin and Wenshu grew ever closer. He had Wenshu's son Shiji marry the Princess of Nanyang, and the rewards that followed were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 及晉王為皇太子，以述為左衛率。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became Crown Prince, he appointed Shu as Colonel of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, he appointed Wenshu Colonel of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 舊令，率官第四品，上以述素貴，遂進率品為第三，其見重如此。

translations.literal: By old regulation the colonel's office was fourth rank; the sovereign, because Shu had long been eminent, therefore advanced the colonel's rank to third—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation the colonel's post was fourth rank, but because Wenshu had long been eminent the emperor raised the colonel's rank to third. Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜左衛大將軍，改封許國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he appointed Shu General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and changed his enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he appointed Wenshu General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and changed his title to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: ，加開府儀同三司，每冬正朝會，輒給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the title of Grand Master with the Ceremonial of Three Insignia, and at each winter court assembly he was granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted the title of Grand Master with the Ceremonial of Three Insignia, and at each winter court assembly he was given a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 從幸榆林，時鐵勒契弊歌棱攻敗吐谷渾，其部攜散，遂遣使請降求救。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor on a visit to Yulin; at that time the Tiele chief Qibi Geleng attacked and defeated Tuyuhun, whose tribes scattered in flight, whereupon they sent envoys to request surrender and aid.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Yulin. At that time the Tiele chief Qibi Geleng attacked and defeated Tuyuhun, whose tribes scattered, and they sent envoys to surrender and beg for rescue.

sentences.zh: 帝令述以兵屯西平之臨羌城，撫納降附。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Shu to station troops at Linyang city in Xiping to comfort and receive those who surrendered and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wenshu to station troops at Linyang in Xiping to receive and pacify those who came over.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾見述擁強兵，懼不敢降，遂西遁。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun, seeing that Shu commanded a strong army, feared and dared not surrender, and therefore fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wenshu's strong force, Tuyuhun was afraid to surrender and fled west.

sentences.zh: 述領鷹揚郎將梁元禮、張峻、崔師等追之，至曼頭城，攻拔之，斬三千餘級。

translations.literal: Shu led the Eagle-Flying Commandants Liang Yuanli, Zhang Jun, Cui Shi, and others in pursuit; reaching Mantou city, he attacked and took it, beheading more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu led the Eagle-Flying commandants Liang Yuanli, Zhang Jun, Cui Shi, and others in pursuit. At Mantou city he stormed and took it, killing more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 乘勝至赤水城，複拔之。

translations.literal: Riding victory he reached Chishui city and again took it.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, he reached Chishui city and took that as well.

sentences.zh: 其餘黨走屯丘尼川，述進擊，大破之，獲其王公、尚書、將軍二百人，前後虜男女四千口而還。

translations.literal: The remaining factions fled and encamped at Qiuni River; Shu advanced and attacked, inflicting a great defeat, capturing two hundred of their kings, dukes, Masters of Writing, and generals, and before and after taking captive four thousand men and women, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled to Qiuni River. Wenshu attacked and routed them, capturing two hundred of their princes, ministers, and generals and, in all, four thousand men and women before returning.

sentences.zh: 渾主南走雪山，其故地皆空。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south to Snow Mountain, and his former lands were all empty.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south toward Snow Mountain, and his former lands were left empty.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 明年，從帝西幸，巡至金山，登燕支，述每為斥候。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Emperor on a western tour to Jinshan, ascended Yanzhi, and Shu each time served as scout.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he accompanied the emperor on a western tour as far as Jinshan and Yanzhi, serving each time as advance scout.

sentences.zh: 時渾賊複寇張掖，進擊走之。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun bandits again raided Zhangye; he advanced, attacked, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raiders again threatened Zhangye, he advanced and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 還至江都宮，敕述與蘇威常典選舉，參預朝政。

translations.literal: Returning to the Jiangdu Palace, the Emperor ordered Shu and Su Wei regularly to preside over selection and appointment and to participate in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the Jiangdu palace, the emperor ordered Wenshu and Su Wei to oversee appointments regularly and to take part in court governance.

sentences.zh: 述時貴重，委任與蘇威等，其親愛則過之。

translations.literal: Shu at that time was eminent and honored; his commission of trust was equal to Su Wei and the rest, but in personal affection he surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was then at the height of honor and power. His formal authority matched Su Wei's, but the emperor's personal affection for him went further.

sentences.zh: 帝所得遠方貢獻及四時口味，輒見班賜，中使相望於道。

translations.literal: Whatever the Emperor received in tribute from distant regions and seasonal delicacies, he would at once bestow portions on him; palace envoys were visible one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever tribute arrived from distant lands or seasonal delicacies the emperor received, he at once sent a share to Wenshu, and palace envoys lined the road between them.

sentences.zh: 述善於供奉，俯仰折旋，容止便辟，宿衛者鹹取則焉。

translations.literal: Shu was skilled at attendance and service; in bowing and rising, turning and wheeling, his bearing and deportment were nimble and obsequious, and those on night guard all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu excelled at court service. In every bow and turn his bearing was nimble and obliging, and the palace guards all took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 又有巧思，凡有所裝飾，皆出人意表。

translations.literal: He also had ingenious thought; whatever he adorned all exceeded people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ingenious in design, and whatever he devised for ornament always surprised people.

sentences.zh: 數以奇服異物進獻宮掖，由是帝彌悅焉。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented strange garments and exotic objects to the inner palace, and thereby the Emperor was ever more pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: He often presented rare garments and curios to the inner palace, and the emperor grew ever more pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 時述貴幸，言無不從，勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Shu was favored and honored; in speech none of his words went unheeded, and his power overshadowed the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of his favor nothing he said went unheeded, and his power overshadowed the court.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍張瑾與述連官，嘗有評議，偶不中意，述張目叱之，瑾惶懼而走，文武百僚莫敢違忤。

translations.literal: General of the Left Guard Zhang Jin served in the same office as Shu; they once had a discussion in which Jin by chance did not please him. Shu glared and shouted at him; Jin fled in fear and alarm, and the civil and military hundred officials dared not disobey or oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin, General of the Left Guard, served in the same office and once disagreed with him on a matter of policy. Wenshu glared and shouted him down. Jin fled in terror, and none of the civil or military officials dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 然性貪鄙，知人有珍異之物，必求取之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was greedy and base; if he knew someone had rare and exotic objects, he was sure to seek and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy and base by nature. If he learned that someone possessed a rare treasure, he was sure to obtain it.

sentences.zh: 富商大賈及隴右諸胡子弟，述皆接以恩意，呼之為兒。

translations.literal: Great merchants and wealthy traders and the sons and younger brothers of the various Hu of Longyou—Shu received them all with gracious intent and called them 'son.'
translations.idiomatic: He treated great merchants and the sons of the Hu families of Longyou with gracious familiarity and called them his sons.

sentences.zh: 由是競加饋遺，金寶累積。

translations.literal: Thereupon they vied in adding gifts, and gold and jewels piled up.
translations.idiomatic: They vied to send him gifts, and gold and jewels piled up around him.

sentences.zh: 後庭曳羅綺者數百，家僮千餘人，皆控良馬，被服金玉。

translations.literal: In the rear courtyard several hundred trailed silk and brocade; household servants numbered more than a thousand, all riding fine horses and clad in gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred women in silk and brocade filled his rear courtyard. More than a thousand household servants rode fine horses and wore gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 述之寵遇，當時莫與為比。

translations.literal: The favor and treatment accorded Shu at that time had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: No one in his day matched the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 及征高麗，述為扶餘道軍將。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Goguryeo was launched, Shu was army commander of the Fuyu Route.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Goguryeo began, Wenshu was made army commander of the Fuyu Route.

sentences.zh: 臨發，帝謂述曰：「禮，七十者行役以婦人從，公宜以家累自隨。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the Emperor said to Shu: 'By ritual, when a man of seventy goes on campaign his wife may accompany him. Lord, you ought to bring your household dependents with you.'
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, the emperor told him, 'By ritual, a man of seventy on campaign may take his wife along. You ought to bring your household with you.'

sentences.zh: 古稱婦人不入軍，謂臨戰時耳。

translations.literal: The ancients said women do not enter the army—this refers only to the moment of battle.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said women do not enter the army, but that meant only at the moment of battle.

sentences.zh: 至於營壘之間，無所傷也。

translations.literal: As for within camps and fortifications, there is no harm in it.
translations.idiomatic: Within the camp there is no harm in it.

sentences.zh: 項籍虞姬，即其故事。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu and Yu Ji are exactly such a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu and Yu Ji are the classic example.'

sentences.zh: 」述與九軍至鴨綠水，糧盡，議欲班師。

translations.literal: Shu and the nine armies reached the Yalu River; provisions were exhausted, and they discussed withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu and the nine armies reached the Yalu River. Provisions ran out, and they debated withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 諸將多異同，述又不測帝意。

translations.literal: The generals were mostly divided in opinion, and Shu also could not fathom the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were divided, and Wenshu could not discern the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 會乙支文德來詣其營，述先與于仲文俱奉密旨，令誘執文德。

translations.literal: It happened that Ye Gaewen came to his camp; Shu had earlier, together with Yu Zhongwen, received a secret edict ordering them to lure and seize Gaewen.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Gaewen came to his camp. Wenshu and Yu Zhongwen had earlier received a secret order to lure and seize him.

sentences.zh: 既而緩縱，文德逃歸，語在《仲文傳》。

translations.literal: Afterward they relaxed and let him go; Gaewen escaped and returned—the account is in the 'Biography of Zhongwen.'
translations.idiomatic: They then relaxed their guard, and Gaewen escaped—the account is given in the biography of Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 述內不自安，遂與諸將渡水追之。

translations.literal: Shu inwardly was ill at ease and thereupon, with the generals, crossed the river in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his own mind, Wenshu crossed the river with the generals in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時文德見述軍中多饑色，欲疲述眾，每鬥便北。

translations.literal: At that time Gaewen saw that many in Shu's army showed the hue of hunger; wishing to wear out Shu's host, each time they fought he at once retreated north.
translations.idiomatic: Gaewen saw that many in Wenshu's army showed hunger in their faces. Hoping to wear them down, he retreated north after every skirmish.

sentences.zh: 述一日之中七戰皆捷，既恃驟勝，又內逼群議，於是遂進，東濟薩水，去平壤城三十裡，因山為營。

translations.literal: In one day Shu fought seven battles and all were victories; relying on sudden triumph and also inwardly pressed by the generals' opinions, he thereupon advanced, crossed east over the Sa River, was thirty li from Pyongyang city, and made camp against the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day Wenshu won seven battles. Trusting in swift victory and pressed by his officers, he advanced, crossed the Sa River to the east, camped thirty li from Pyongyang against the mountainside.

sentences.zh: 文德複遣使偽降，請述曰：「若旋師者，當奉高元朝行在所。

translations.literal: Gaewen again sent envoys with a false surrender, requesting Shu: 'If you withdraw the army, we will present King Goguryeo at your marching headquarters.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaewen sent envoys with a feigned offer of surrender, saying, 'If you withdraw, we will deliver King Goguryeo to your headquarters.'

sentences.zh: 」述見士卒疲敝，不可複戰，又平壤險固，卒難致力，遂因其詐而還。

translations.literal: Shu saw that the soldiers were weary and exhausted and could not fight again, and that Pyongyang was perilous and strong and could not quickly be taken by force; he therefore accepted their deception and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu saw that his troops were exhausted and could fight no more, and that Pyongyang was strong and could not quickly be taken. He accepted the ruse and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 眾半濟，賊擊後軍，於是大潰，不可禁止，九軍敗績，一日一夜，還至鴨綠水，行四百五十裡。

translations.literal: When the host was half across, the bandits struck the rear army; thereupon came a great rout that could not be stopped. The nine armies were defeated; in one day and one night they returned to the Yalu River, traveling four hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: When half the army was across, the enemy struck the rear. A rout followed that could not be stopped. All nine armies were shattered. In one day and one night they fled back to the Yalu, covering four hundred fifty li.

sentences.zh: 初，渡遼九軍三十萬五千人，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人。

translations.literal: Initially the nine armies crossing Liao had three hundred five thousand men; when they returned to Liaodong city, only two thousand seven hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: The nine armies had numbered three hundred five thousand when they crossed the Liao. When they returned to Liaodong city, only twenty-seven hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，以述等屬吏。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and handed Shu and the others over to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and handed Wenshu and the others over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 至東都，除名為民。

translations.literal: Reaching the Eastern Capital, they were stripped of rank and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital they were stripped of rank and reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝有事遼東，複述官爵，待之如初。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Emperor had business in Liaodong, he restored Shu's offices and titles and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor again campaigned in Liaodong, he restored Wenshu's offices and titles and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 從至遼東，與將軍楊義臣率兵複臨鴨綠水。

translations.literal: He followed to Liaodong and, with the general Yang Yichen, led troops again to the banks of the Yalu.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Liaodong and, with the general Yang Yichen, again brought troops to the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感作亂，帝召述班師，令馳驛赴河陽，發諸郡兵以討玄感。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Xuangan raised rebellion; the Emperor summoned Shu to withdraw the army and ordered him to ride post-haste to Heyang, mobilizing troops from the various commanderies to attack Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan rebelled. The emperor recalled Wenshu, ordered him to ride post-haste to Heyang, and raise troops from the commanderies to crush Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 時玄感逼東都，聞述軍將至，懼而西遁，將圖關中。

translations.literal: At that time Xuangan was pressing the Eastern Capital; hearing that Shu's army was about to arrive, he was afraid and fled west, intending to take Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan was then pressing the Eastern Capital. When he heard Wenshu was coming, he fled west, intending to seize Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 述與刑部尚書衛玄、左禦衛將軍來護兒、武衛將軍屈突通等躡之。

translations.literal: Shu, together with Minister of Justice Wei Xuan, General of the Left Imperial Guard Lai Huer, General of the Martial Guard Qu Tu Tong, and others, pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu pursued him with the Minister of Justice Wei Xuan, General of the Left Imperial Guard Lai Huer, General of the Martial Guard Qu Tu Tong, and others.

sentences.zh: 至閿鄉皇天原，與玄感相及。

translations.literal: Reaching Huangtian Plain in Wenxiang, they caught up with Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangtian Plain in Wenxiang they caught up with Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 述與來護兒列陣當其前，遣屈突通以奇兵擊其後，大破之，遂斬玄感，傳首行在所。

translations.literal: Shu and Lai Huer drew up battle lines before him, sent Qu Tu Tong with a surprise force to strike his rear, inflicted a great defeat, then beheaded Xuangan and sent his head to the Emperor's traveling headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu and Lai Huer formed the front line while Qu Tu Tong struck from the rear with a flanking force. They routed Xuangan, beheaded him, and sent his head to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 賜物數千段。

translations.literal: He was granted several thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with several thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 複從東征，至懷遠而還。

translations.literal: He again followed on the eastern campaign, reaching Huaiyuan and returning.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the eastern campaign, advancing as far as Huaiyuan before returning.

sentences.zh: 突厥之圍雁門，帝懼，述請潰圍而出。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, the Emperor was afraid; Shu requested to break out of the encirclement and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, the emperor was afraid. Wenshu urged a breakout.

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋固諫不可，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai firmly remonstrated that it could not be done, and the Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai firmly dissuaded him, and the emperor abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，車駕次太原，議者多勸帝還京師，帝有難色。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, the imperial carriage halted at Taiyuan; many in council urged the Emperor to return to the capital, and the Emperor showed a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted, the court halted at Taiyuan. Many advisers urged a return to the capital, but the emperor looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 述因奏曰：「從官妻子多在東都，便道向洛陽，自潼關而入可也。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon memorialized: 'The wives and children of the attendant officials are mostly in the Eastern Capital; we may take the convenient route toward Luoyang and enter through Tong Pass.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu memorialized, 'The wives and children of your attendants are mostly in the Eastern Capital. We could take the convenient route to Luoyang and enter through Tong Pass.'

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，至東都，述又觀望帝意，勸幸江都，帝大悅。

translations.literal: That year, reaching the Eastern Capital, Shu again watched the Emperor's intent and urged a visit to Jiangdu; the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after reaching the Eastern Capital, Wenshu read the emperor's mood and urged a journey to Jiangdu. The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 述于江都遇疾，中使相望，帝將親臨視之，群臣苦諫乃止。

translations.literal: Shu fell ill at Jiangdu; palace envoys were visible one after another. The Emperor was about to visit him in person, but the ministers earnestly remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu fell ill at Jiangdu, and palace envoys came and went in steady succession. The emperor was about to visit him in person, but the ministers dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 遂遣司宮魏氏問述曰：「必有不諱，欲何所言？

translations.literal: He thereupon sent the Palace Stewardess of the Wei clan to ask Shu: 'You must have something you cannot speak of—what do you wish to say?'
translations.idiomatic: He sent the palace stewardess of the Wei clan to ask, 'You must have something on your mind—what do you wish to say?'

sentences.zh: 」述二子化及、智及，時並得罪於家，述因奏曰：「化及臣之長子，早預籓邸，願陛下哀憐之。

translations.literal: Shu's two sons Huaji and Zhiji at that time had both offended at home. Shu thereupon memorialized: 'Huaji is my eldest son; he early entered the prince's household. I beg Your Majesty to show him pity.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu's sons Huaji and Zhiji had both fallen from favor at home. He memorialized, 'Huaji is my eldest son. He entered the prince's household long ago. I beg Your Majesty to show him mercy.'

sentences.zh: 」帝聞，泫然曰：「吾不忘也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he said with tears: 'I will not forget.'
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor said through tears, 'I will not forget.'

sentences.zh: 」及薨，帝為之廢朝，贈司徒、尚書令、十郡太守，班劍四十人，轀輬車，前後部鼓吹，諡曰恭，帝令黃門侍郎裴矩祭乙太牢，鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: When he died, the Emperor suspended court for him, posthumously granted him Grand Tutor, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of ten commanderies, forty attendants with ceremonial swords, an imperial funeral carriage, martial music before and behind, and the posthumous title Gong. The Emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant-Minister Pei Ju to sacrifice with the second-grade great offering, and the Director of Ceremonial to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor suspended court. He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Director of the Masters of Writing, granted the governorship of ten commanderies, forty sword attendants, an imperial funeral carriage, and martial music before and behind. His posthumous title was Gong. The emperor ordered Pei Ju to sacrifice with the second-grade great offering and the Director of Ceremonial to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 子化及，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Huaji has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaji is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 雲定興雲定興者，附會於述。

translations.literal: Yun Dingxing—Yun Dingxing attached himself to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Dingxing attached himself to Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 初，定興女為皇太子勇昭訓，及勇廢，除名配少府。

translations.literal: Initially Dingxing's daughter was Brilliant Instruction to Crown Prince Yong; when Yong was deposed, she was struck from the rolls and assigned to the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dingxing's daughter had been Brilliant Instruction to Crown Prince Yong. When Yong was deposed, she was struck from the rolls and assigned to the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 定興先得昭訓明珠絡帳，私賂於述，自是數共交遊。

translations.literal: Dingxing had earlier obtained the Brilliant Instruction's pearl-net canopy and privately bribed Shu with it; from then on they frequently associated together.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing had earlier obtained the Brilliant Instruction's pearl-net canopy and privately bribed Wenshu with it. From then on they associated frequently.

sentences.zh: 定興每時節必有賂遺，並以音樂幹述。

translations.literal: At every season Dingxing was sure to send gifts, and also used music to please Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At every season Dingxing sent gifts, and he also used music to win Wenshu's favor.

sentences.zh: 述素好著奇服，炫耀時人。

translations.literal: Shu had long loved wearing strange garments and dazzling the men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu had long loved outlandish dress and dazzling his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 定興為制馬韉，於後角上缺方三寸，以露白色。

translations.literal: Dingxing made a saddle for him with a square three inches across cut out of the rear corner to expose white.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing made him a saddle with a three-inch square cut from the rear corner to expose white underneath.

sentences.zh: 世輕薄者爭放學之，謂為許公缺勢。

translations.literal: The frivolous men of the age vied to imitate it, calling it the Duke of Xu's missing corner.
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous men of the age vied to copy it, calling it the Duke of Xu's missing corner.

sentences.zh: 又遇天寒，定興曰：「入內宿衛，必當耳冷。

translations.literal: Again, when the weather turned cold, Dingxing said: 'When entering the palace on night guard, the ears must surely grow cold.'
translations.idiomatic: When the weather turned cold, Dingxing said, 'On night duty inside the palace, your ears must surely grow cold.'

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「然。

translations.literal: Shu said: 'So it is.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu said, 'Indeed.'

sentences.zh: 」乃制裌頭巾，令深袙耳。

translations.literal: He thereupon made a lined headcloth designed to wrap deeply over the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing then made a lined headcloth designed to wrap deeply over the ears.

sentences.zh: 又學之，名為許公袙勢。

translations.literal: Others again imitated it, calling it the Duke of Xu's wrapped-ear style.
translations.idiomatic: Others copied it too, calling it the Duke of Xu's wrapped-ear style.

sentences.zh: 述大悅曰：「雲兄所作，必能變俗。

translations.literal: Shu was greatly pleased and said: 'What Brother Yun has made will surely transform custom.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was delighted and said, 'What Brother Yun has made will surely change fashion.'

sentences.zh: 我聞作事可法，故不虛也。

translations.literal: I have heard that what one makes can become a model—so it is not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that what one makes can set a standard for others. This is no empty boast.'

sentences.zh: 」後帝將事四夷，大造兵器，述薦之，因敕少府工匠並取其節度。

translations.literal: Later, when the Emperor was about to undertake affairs with the four barbarian directions and was greatly manufacturing weapons, Shu recommended him, and the Emperor therefore ordered the craftsmen of the Palace Storehouse all to follow his standards.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor prepared campaigns against the frontier peoples and greatly expanded arms production, Wenshu recommended him. The emperor ordered the Palace Storehouse craftsmen to follow his standards.

sentences.zh: 述欲為之求官，謂定興曰：「兄所制器仗併合上心，而不得官者，為長寧兄弟猶未死耳。

translations.literal: Shu wished to obtain office for him and said to Dingxing: 'The arms and equipment you make all suit the sovereign's heart, yet you cannot obtain office because the brothers of Changning are still not dead.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu wanted office for him and told Dingxing, 'The arms you make all please the emperor, yet you cannot obtain office because the Changning brothers are still alive.'

sentences.zh: 」定興曰：「此無用物，何不勸上殺之。

translations.literal: Dingxing said: 'These useless creatures—why not urge the sovereign to kill them?'
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing said, 'Those useless men—why not urge the emperor to kill them?'

sentences.zh: 」述因奏曰：「房陵諸子，年並成立。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon memorialized: 'The sons at Fangling have all reached maturity in years.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu memorialized, 'The sons at Fangling have all come of age.

sentences.zh: 今欲動兵征討，若將從駕，則守掌為難；

translations.literal: Now, wishing to mobilize troops for campaign, if they are taken along with the imperial carriage, guarding and holding will be difficult;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now mobilizes for campaign and they accompany the court, guarding them will be difficult;

sentences.zh: 若留一處，又恐不可。

translations.literal: if they are left in one place, again there is fear that it will not do.
translations.idiomatic: if they are left behind, that too is dangerous.

sentences.zh: 進退無用，請早處分。

translations.literal: Whether advancing or withdrawing they are useless—please dispose of them early.
translations.idiomatic: They serve no purpose either way. Please deal with them at once.'

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，因鴆殺長寧，又遣以下七弟分配嶺表，仍遣間使于路盡殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this and therefore poisoned Changning; he also sent the seven younger brothers below him to be distributed across Lingnan, and still sent secret agents on the road to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. He poisoned Changning and sent the seven younger brothers into exile in Lingnan, then had secret agents kill them all on the road.

sentences.zh: 五年，大閱軍實，帝稱甲仗為佳。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, a great review of military stores was held; the Emperor praised the armor and weapons as excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a great review of military stores was held, and the emperor praised the armor and weapons as excellent.

sentences.zh: 述奏曰：」並雲定興之功也。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: 'This is entirely the achievement of Yun Dingxing.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu memorialized, 'This is entirely Yun Dingxing's achievement.'

sentences.zh: 」擢授少府丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing was promoted to Assistant Director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 尋代何稠為少監，轉衛尉少卿，遷左禦衛將軍，仍知少府事。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced He Chou as Junior Director, was transferred to Junior Minister of the Guard, was promoted to General of the Left Imperial Guard, and still oversaw Palace Storehouse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced He Chou as Junior Director, became Junior Minister of the Guard, was made General of the Left Imperial Guard, and still oversaw Palace Storehouse affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 凡述所薦達，皆至大官。

translations.literal: All whom Shu recommended and advanced reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone Wenshu recommended rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 趙行樞乙太常樂戶，家財億計，述謂為兄，多受其賄。

translations.literal: Zhao Xingshu, a music-house man of the Grand Music Office, had household wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions; Shu called him brother and received many bribes from him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingshu, a music-house man of the Grand Music Office, had household wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions. Wenshu called him brother and took many bribes from him.

sentences.zh: 稱其驍勇，起家為折衝郎將。

translations.literal: Calling him fierce and brave, he began his career as Colonel Who Breaks the Charge.
translations.idiomatic: Praising his valor, Wenshu had him begin his career as Colonel Who Breaks the Charge.

sentences.zh: 郭衍郭衍，字彥文，自雲太原介休人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yan—Guo Yan, style name Yanwen, claimed to be a native of Jiexiu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan, whose courtesy name was Yanwen, claimed descent from Jiexiu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父以舍人從魏武帝入關，其後官至侍中。

translations.literal: His father, as an attendant, followed Emperor Wu of Wei in entering the passes; afterward he reached the office of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father had followed Emperor Wu of Wei into the passes as an attendant and later rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 衍少驍武，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yan in youth was fierce in martial prowess and skilled in riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yan was bold in arms and skilled in riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 周陳王純引為左右，累遷大都督。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Chun of Zhou brought him in as a close attendant, and he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chen Chun of Zhou took him as a close attendant, and he rose in stages to Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 時齊氏未平，衍奉詔於天水募人，以鎮東境，得樂徙千餘家，屯於陝城。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi house was not yet pacified; Yan received an edict to recruit men at Tianshui to garrison the eastern border, obtaining more than a thousand households of music-house migrants, whom he stationed at Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: While the Northern Qi had not yet been subdued, Yan was ordered to recruit men at Tianshui to guard the eastern frontier. He settled more than a thousand music-house migrant households at Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 拜使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand Master with the Ceremonial of Three Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand Master with the Ceremonial of Three Insignia.

sentences.zh: 每有寇至，輒率所領禦之，一歲數告捷，頗為齊人所憚。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits came, he would lead those under his command to repel them; within a year he reported victory several times and was rather feared by the men of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever raiders appeared, he led his men against them. Within a year he reported several victories and came to be feared by the Qi.

sentences.zh: 王益親任之。

translations.literal: The Prince increasingly favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince came to favor and trust him ever more.

sentences.zh: 建德中，周武帝出幸雲陽，衍朝於行所，時議欲伐齊，衍請為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era, Emperor Wu of Zhou went on tour to Yunyang; Yan attended at the traveling headquarters. At that time council favored attacking Qi, and Yan requested to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era Emperor Wu of Zhou visited Yunyang, and Yan attended him there. When the court debated an attack on Qi, Yan asked to lead the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 攻河陰城，授儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Attacking Heyin city, he was appointed Grand General with the Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Heyin city and was appointed Grand General with the Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 武帝圍晉州，慮齊兵來援，令衍從陳王守千里徑。

translations.literal: The Emperor besieged Jin Province, fearing that Qi troops would come to its aid, and ordered Yan to follow Prince Chen in guarding the Thousand-Li Path.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor besieged Jin Province, fearing Qi reinforcements, he had Yan follow Prince Chen in guarding the Thousand-Li Path.

sentences.zh: 又從武帝與齊主大戰于晉州，追齊師至高壁，敗之。

translations.literal: He again followed the Emperor in the great battle with the Qi ruler at Jin Province, pursued the Qi army to Gaobi, and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the emperor in the great battle with the Qi ruler at Jin Province, pursued the Qi army to Gaobi, and defeated it.

sentences.zh: 仍從平并州，以功加授開府，封武強縣公，邑一千二百戶，賜姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: He still followed in the pacification of Bing Province; for his merit he was additionally granted Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang County with a fief of twelve hundred households, and granted the surname Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the pacification of Bing Province and, for his service, was further granted Grand Master of the Palace, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang with a fief of twelve hundred households, and given the surname Chiluo.

sentences.zh: ，為右中軍熊渠中大夫。

translations.literal: He became Valiant Channel Grand Master of the Right Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Valiant Channel Grand Master of the Right Central Army.

sentences.zh: 尉迥之起逆，從韋孝寬戰于武陟，進戰於相州。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi Kuo raised rebellion, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in battle at Wuzhi and advanced to fight at Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Jue rebelled, he fought under Wei Xiaokuan at Wuzhi and advanced to battle at Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，迥遣弟子勤為青州總管，率青、齊之眾來助迥。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kuo had sent his younger brother's son Qin as Commander-in-Chief of Qing Province, leading the hosts of Qing and Qi to aid Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jue had sent his nephew Qin as Commander-in-Chief of Qing Province to lead the forces of Qing and Qi to his aid.

sentences.zh: 迥敗，勤與迥子惇、祐等欲東奔青州。

translations.literal: When Kuo was defeated, Qin together with Kuo's sons Dun, You, and others wished to flee east to Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Jue was defeated, Qin and Jue's sons Dun, You, and others tried to flee east to Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 衍將精騎一千追破之，執祐於陣，勤遂遁走，而惇亦逃逸。

translations.literal: Yan led a thousand elite cavalry in pursuit, defeated them, seized You on the battlefield, whereupon Qin fled, while Dun also escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yan pursued with a thousand elite horsemen, routed them, and seized You on the field. Qin fled, and Dun escaped as well.

sentences.zh: 衍至濟州，入據其城，又擊其餘党於濟北，累戰破之，執送京師。

translations.literal: Yan reached Ji Province, entered and seized its city, again struck their remaining factions in Jibei, repeatedly fought and defeated them, seized them and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reached Ji Province, took the city, and struck the remaining rebels in Jibei. After repeated victories he sent the captives to the capital.

sentences.zh: 超授上柱國，封武山郡公。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wushan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted out of turn to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wushan.

sentences.zh: 賞物七千段。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with seven thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He received seven thousand lengths of goods as reward.

sentences.zh: 密勸高祖殺周室諸王，早行禪代。

translations.literal: He secretly urged Gaozu to kill the princes of the Zhou house and carry out the abdication and succession early.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Yang Jian to kill the Zhou princes and complete the abdication and succession at once.

sentences.zh: 由是大被親昵。

translations.literal: Thereby he came to be greatly favored and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won great favor and intimacy.

sentences.zh: ，敕復舊姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: An edict restored his original surname as Guo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his original surname of Guo.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，以衍為行軍總管，領兵屯於平涼。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was made campaign commander-in-chief and led troops stationed at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was made campaign commander-in-chief and stationed troops at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，虜不入。

translations.literal: For several years the barbarians did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: For several years the barbarians did not cross the border.

sentences.zh: 征為開漕渠大監。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Grand Director of Opening the Transport Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Grand Director of Opening the Transport Canal.

sentences.zh: 部率水工，鑿渠引渭水，經大興城北，東至於潼關，漕運四百餘裡。

translations.literal: He directed and led the water workers, cut a canal to draw the Wei River, passed north of Daxing city, and extended east to Tong Pass—a transport route of more than four hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the water workers in cutting a canal to draw the Wei River past the north of Daxing and east to Tong Pass, a transport route of more than four hundred li.

sentences.zh: 關內賴之，名之曰富民渠。

translations.literal: Within the passes they relied on it, and it was named the Canal for Enriching the People.
translations.idiomatic: The region within the passes relied on it, and it was named the Canal for Enriching the People.

sentences.zh: 五年，授瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 遇秋霖大水，其屬縣多漂沒，民皆上高樹，依大家。

translations.literal: He encountered autumn rains and great floods; many subordinate counties were washed away, and the people all climbed tall trees and relied on great households.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn rains brought great floods. Many counties under his jurisdiction were inundated, and people climbed tall trees or took refuge with wealthy households.

sentences.zh: 衍親備舩栰，並齎糧拯救之，民多獲濟。

translations.literal: Yan personally prepared boats and rafts, and together brought grain to rescue them; many among the people were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Yan personally prepared boats and rafts, brought grain, and rescued them. Many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 衍先開倉賑恤，後始聞奏。

translations.literal: Yan first opened the granaries for relief before he memorialized and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Yan opened the granaries for relief before he reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上大善之，選授朔州總管。

translations.literal: The sovereign greatly approved of this and selected him for appointment as Commander-in-Chief of Shuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved and appointed him Commander-in-Chief of Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 所部有恆安鎮，北接蕃境，常勞轉運。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction was Heng'an garrison, which on the north adjoined the barbarian border and constantly labored under transport duties.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction included Heng'an garrison on the northern frontier, where transport duties were a constant burden.

sentences.zh: 衍乃選沃饒地，置屯田，歲剩粟萬餘石，民免轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon selected fertile land and established military colonies; each year surplus grain exceeded ten thousand piculs, and the people were spared the labor of transport.
translations.idiomatic: Yan selected fertile land and established military colonies. Each year more than ten thousand piculs of surplus grain were produced, sparing the people transport labor.

sentences.zh: 又築桑乾鎮，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He also built Sanggan garrison—all met with imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: He also built Sanggan garrison. All met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 十年，從晉王廣出鎮揚州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Prince of Jin Guang in going out to garrison Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he followed Prince Jin Guang to his posting at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇江表構逆，命衍為總管，領精銳萬人先屯京口。

translations.literal: When the lower Yangtze region raised rebellion, he was ordered as commander-in-chief to lead ten thousand elite troops to station first at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower Yangtze rebelled, he was made commander-in-chief and led ten thousand elite troops to station first at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 于貴洲南與賊戰，敗之，生擒魁帥，大獲舟楫糧儲，以充軍實，乃討東陽、永嘉、宣城、黟、歙諸洞，盡平之。

translations.literal: South of Guizhou he fought the bandits, defeated them, captured the chieftains alive, and greatly obtained boats, grain stores, and supplies to fill the army's needs; he then attacked the caves of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She, and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: South of Guizhou he defeated the rebels, captured their leaders alive, and seized boats, grain, and supplies for the army. He then subdued the mountain strongholds of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She.

sentences.zh: 授蔣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 衍臨下甚踞，事上奸諂。

translations.literal: Yan toward those below was very overbearing; toward his superiors he was sycophantic and flattering.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was overbearing toward those below and sycophantic toward his superiors.

sentences.zh: 晉王愛昵之，宴賜隆厚。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin loved and favored him; feasts and gifts were lavish and thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin favored him and lavished feasts and gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 遷洪州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Hong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Hong Province.

sentences.zh: 王有奪宗之謀，托衍心腹，遣宇文述以情告之。

translations.literal: The Prince had a plot to seize the heirship and entrusted Yan as a confidant; he sent Yu Wen Shu to tell him his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: The prince secretly plotted to seize the succession and made Yan his confidant, sending Yu Wenshu to confide in him.

sentences.zh: 衍大喜曰：「若所謀事果，自可為皇太子。

translations.literal: Yan was greatly pleased and said: 'If the affair you plot succeeds, you may naturally become Crown Prince.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan was delighted and said, 'If your plot succeeds, you may naturally become crown prince.

sentences.zh: 如其不諧，亦須據淮海，複梁、陳之舊。

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, you must still hold Huaihai and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, you must still hold the Huaihai region and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.

sentences.zh: 副君酒客，其如我何？

translations.literal: What can the crown prince's wine-companion do to me?'
translations.idiomatic: What can the crown prince's drinking companion do to me?'

sentences.zh: 」王因召衍，陰共計議。

translations.literal: The Prince thereupon summoned Yan and secretly plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: The prince summoned Yan and they plotted together in secret.

sentences.zh: 又恐人疑無故來往，托以衍妻患癭，王妃蕭氏有術能療之。

translations.literal: Again fearing that people would suspect their coming and going without cause, they used as a pretext that Yan's wife suffered from goiter and that the princess consort of the Xiao clan had skill to cure it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing suspicion over their frequent visits, they claimed that Yan's wife suffered from goiter and that Princess Xiao knew how to cure it.

sentences.zh: 以狀奏高祖，高祖聽衍共妻向江都，往來無度。

translations.literal: They memorialized the situation to Gaozu; Gaozu permitted Yan to bring his wife to Jiangdu, and their coming and going was without limit.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized Gaozu, who permitted Yan to bring his wife to Jiangdu. Their visits became constant.

sentences.zh: 衍又詐稱桂州俚反，王乃奏衍行兵討之。

translations.literal: Yan again falsely claimed that the Li of Gui Province had rebelled; the Prince thereupon memorialized that Yan should lead troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also falsely reported a Li rebellion in Gui Province, and the prince memorialized that Yan should lead troops to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 由是大修甲仗，陰養士卒。

translations.literal: Thereby he greatly repaired armor and weapons and secretly nurtured soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On this pretext he greatly expanded arms production and secretly trained troops.

sentences.zh: 及王入為太子，征授左監門率，轉左宗衛率。

translations.literal: When the Prince entered the capital as Crown Prince, Yan was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Left Gate Guard, then transferred to Colonel of the Left Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Yan was summoned and appointed Colonel of the Left Gate Guard, then Colonel of the Left Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖于仁壽宮將大漸，太子與楊素矯詔，令衍、宇文述領東宮兵，帖上臺宿衛，門禁並由之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu at Renshou Palace was about to reach his last stage, the Crown Prince and Yang Su forged an edict ordering Yan and Yu Wen Shu to lead the Eastern Palace troops, post them as night guards on the upper terrace, and put gate control entirely in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu lay dying at Renshou Palace, the crown prince and Yang Su forged an edict placing the Eastern Palace troops under Yan and Yu Wenshu. They posted guards on the upper terrace and controlled every gate.

sentences.zh: 及上崩，漢王起逆，而京師空虛，使衍馳還，總兵居守。

translations.literal: When the sovereign died, Prince of Han raised rebellion while the capital was empty; Yan was sent to ride back in haste and take overall command to hold and defend.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Prince Han rebelled while the capital was undefended. Yan was sent back in haste to take command and hold the city.

sentences.zh: ，拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，令衍統左軍，改授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Jiangdu, he ordered Yan to command the left army and changed his appointment to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Jiangdu, he had Yan command the left army and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 又從討吐谷渾，出金山道，納絳二萬餘戶。

translations.literal: He again followed in the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving submission from more than twenty thousand households of the Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and receiving the submission of more than twenty thousand Jiang households.

sentences.zh: 衍能揣上意，阿諛順旨。

translations.literal: Yan was able to gauge the sovereign's intent and fawned and flattered in accord with his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan could read the emperor's mind and fawned upon him in every way.

sentences.zh: 帝每謂人曰：「唯有郭衍，心與朕同。

translations.literal: The Emperor often said to others: 'Only Guo Yan has a heart in accord with Mine.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said, 'Only Guo Yan's heart is one with mine.'

sentences.zh: 」又嘗勸帝取樂，五日一視事，無得效高祖空自劬勞。

translations.literal: He also once urged the Emperor to take pleasure, to attend to affairs once every five days, and not to imitate Gaozu in toiling and laboring in vain.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to enjoy himself, attend to affairs only once every five days, and not imitate Gaozu in wearing himself out with empty toil.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，益稱其孝順。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this and increasingly praised his filial obedience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and praised his filial devotion all the more.

sentences.zh: 初，新令行，衍封爵從例除。

translations.literal: Initially, when the new statutes took effect, Yan's enfeoffment and title were removed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the new statutes took effect, Yan's title was removed according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 六年，以恩幸封真定侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, through favor and grace he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending through imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 七年，從往江都，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed on the journey to Jiangdu and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈左衛大將軍，賵賜甚厚，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General-in-Chief of the Left Guard; funeral gifts were very lavish, and his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard. Funeral gifts were lavish, and his posthumous title was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長子臻，武牙郎將。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhen was Martial Tusk Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhen served as Martial Tusk Commandant.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣本，孝昌縣令。

translations.literal: His second son Siben was Magistrate of Xiaochang County.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Siben was Magistrate of Xiaochang County.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：謇謇匪躬，為臣之高節，和而不同，事君之常道。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Earnest and not sparing oneself is the highest integrity of a minister; harmonious yet not identical is the constant way of serving one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historiographer writes: To be earnest and spare oneself nothing is the highest integrity of a minister; to be harmonious yet not merely agreeable is the constant way of serving one's lord.

sentences.zh: 宇文述、郭衍以水濟水，如脂如韋，便辟足恭，柔顏取悅。

translations.literal: Yu Wen Shu and Guo Yan used water to aid water, were like grease and like leather, nimble and obsequious in foot and bearing, soft of countenance to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu and Guo Yan were like water poured upon water, supple as grease and leather. They were nimble and obsequious in bearing, soft of face, and eager to please.

sentences.zh: 君所謂可，亦曰可焉，君所謂不，亦曰不焉。

translations.literal: What the lord called acceptable, they also called acceptable; what the lord called not, they also called not.
translations.idiomatic: What the lord approved, they approved; what he rejected, they rejected.

sentences.zh: 無所是非，不能輕重，默默苟容，偷安高位，甘素餐之責，受彼己之譏。

translations.literal: They had no right or wrong of their own, could not weigh light and heavy, silently endured in complacency, stole ease in high position, were content with the blame of eating salary without work, and accepted the ridicule of others toward themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They had no judgment of their own, could weigh nothing on their own, silently endured, clung to high office in ease, accepted the shame of drawing salary without service, and bore the scorn of others.

sentences.zh: 此固君子所不為，亦丘明之深恥也。

translations.literal: This is what a gentleman by nature does not do, and it is also what Qiu Ming deeply regarded as shame.
translations.idiomatic: This is what a gentleman will not do, and it is what Qiu Ming deeply regarded as shame.
